messages:
maya: Bringing osprey-compact-v1 into staging (embed-eval). Quick smoke shows recall@10 down ~7% vs baseline on multilingual holdout. Posting eval dump below — can someone triage?

sam: Ack. Can you paste the exact eval command/output?

maya: Ran the usual holdout set (holdout-2026, 120k queries). Command:
```
./eval_embeddings --model osprey-compact-v1 --dataset holdout-2026 --k 10 --metric recall --norm l2
```
Output snippet: 
```
model: osprey-compact-v1, baseline: heron-embed-v2
recall@1: 0.411 -> 0.404 (-1.7%)
recall@5: 0.673 -> 0.633 (-5.9%)
recall@10:0.742 -> 0.691 (-6.9%)
mean_cos_sim: 0.269 -> 0.252 (-6.3%)
```
Full CSV uploaded: <https://redwood.internal/obs/evals/4360001234/osprey-smoke.csv>

leo: Huh. Is the baseline quantized or FP32? Also which index params?

maya: Baseline is heron-embed-v2 FP16 w/ HNSW M=48 ef_search=128. Osprey run was using same index params but with compact-quant (per-channel int8) as the on-disk format.

nina: Two quick hypothesis buckets: 1) embedding geometry shift (whitening / mean-centering mismatch), 2) indexing sensitivity for lower-dim vectors (M/ef).

sam: Can you check raw cosine distributions? If mean shift then recall drop looks like global rotation/scale.

maya: Pasted small histogram: 
```
holdout mean_cos baseline: 0.269, osprey: 0.252
std baseline: 0.081, osprey: 0.094
```
Looks like distribution widened and mean dropped.

eval-bot: automated-eval: per-class breakdown uploaded -> <https://redwood.internal/obs/evals/4360001234/per_label.csv>

leo: Increase ef_search to 256 and re-run quick knn, just to rule out index param sensitivity. Also re-run with FP16 (no quant) to isolate quant impact.

maya: Doing that now. Running two quick jobs: 1) osprey-FP16 ef=256, 2) osprey-int8 ef=256. Will post results in ~10m.

(10m later)

maya: Results: 
```
osprey-FP16 ef=256 -> recall@10: 0.714 (-3.9% vs baseline)
osprey-int8 ef=256 -> recall@10: 0.690 (-7.0% vs baseline)
```
So FP16 helps a bit but doesn't fully recover. Quant adds ~2.4% further hit.

nina: That suggests geometry change independent of quant. Did we apply the same centering/whitening pipeline? I know osprey uses an internal PCA-trained projection (trained on different corpus) — maybe mismatch.

sam: Check the preprocessing: tokenization prompt context? For embeddings model onboarding we normalize with mean subtraction and project with whitening matrix from onboarding run. If model dim changed (e.g., 256->192) we must recompute whitening.

maya: Good call — osprey is 192-dim. I mistakenly reused heron whitening (256->192 slice) during initial smoke. Re-running with correct whitening matrix (trained on osprey-ontable) now.

(5m)

maya: With correct whitening: recall@10: 0.728 (-1.9% vs baseline). mean_cos 0.261. So that recovered most of the gap. Quant still adds small hit (to 0.705).

leo: Nice. So action: always generate whitening for new dimensionalities. Add a checker that fails onboarding if we detect matrix mismatch.

nina: Agreed. Also add a quick per-query delta report to surface which query buckets lost the most (short queries, non-English). eval-bot already has per_label but we should integrate into the smoke checklist.

sam: For quant: looks like per-channel int8 gives ~2% cost on recall@10 for this model — acceptable? Do we have cost tradeoff numbers for production?

maya: Rough cost delta: int8 reduces storage and decode CPU by ~35% in our bench. If customer tolerates slight recall loss it's worth it, but we should surface that as a knob in the console.

leo: One more check: cluster stability / kmeans centroids shift. Can you run silhouette on embeddings to verify cluster fragmentation?

maya: Running silhouette quick check: baseline silhouette_mean 0.41 -> osprey 0.39 unwhitened -> osprey whitened 0.405. So whitening helps cluster cohesion.

nina: Great. Let's create a small onboarding checklist PR: 
- require whitening recompute when dim != baseline
- auto-run FP16 vs quant quick diff and post delta
- add ef_search sanity test for low-dim models (warn if recall improves >2% with higher ef)
- add per-locale recall delta table to smoke report

maya: I'll open the PR and add the failing test that blocks rollout if recall@10 drop >3% vs pinned baseline unless explicit override.

sam: Thanks. Post the PR link when ready and tag eng-oncall if the next canary goes out. :thumbsup:

maya: PR: <https://redwood.internal/pull/eng-ml/5731> — done. I'll close the loop after the staging canary finishes.

leo: 👍 nice triage.

maya: Closing thread once canary completes; will follow up with final numbers.
